title: Hogwarts Pest Control: Cornish Pixie Panic
premise: A Hogwarts student uses enchanted golden tongs to pluck cursed pixies and magical pests off unstable ward maps before the castle's defenses fail.
interaction_model: Single-screen mouse-and-touch drag arcade play. Press a pest, drag it away, and release far enough to banish it.
objective: Maintain ward integrity by clearing magical pests quickly and efficiently for as long as possible.
progression: An endless survival loop with rising pressure, reframed as a five-world Hogwarts outbreak journey from common room training to Great Hall crisis.
theme: Harry Potter-inspired magical castle pest-control emergency.
mood: Whimsical, urgent, magical, and increasingly high-stakes.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the drag-to-clear arcade loop.
High confidence that Harry Potter theming should remain cosmetic and presentational.
Moderate confidence that the central foot artwork should be reinterpreted rather than structurally replaced.
source_game_summary: The source game is a neon bug-clearing arcade game where bugs spawn on a central foot shape and must be dragged away before they drain health.
remix_prompt_interpretation: Translate the bug-removal loop into Hogwarts magical pest control, using wizarding school spaces, ward integrity fiction, and procedural magical art while preserving mechanics.
preserve_elements: score and health reward on successful clear
transform_elements: stage identity into warded magical surface
neon club palette into wizarding world palette progression
reaction cards into magical alert cards
ambient world storytelling into a five-level Hogwarts journey
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly one-screen arcade game called 'Hogwarts Pest Control: Cornish Pixie Panic' where the player acts as a Hogwarts student using enchanted golden tongs to remove cursed pixies and magical pests from a glowing ward map before the castle's protective magic collapses. Preserve the source structure as a drag-to-clear reflex loop: pests spawn on a central magical surface, the player presses or touches a pest, drags it away, and releases far enough to banish it; if pests remain too long, they continuously damage a ward-integrity meter until game over. Keep score as pests banished and allow successful clears to restore some ward strength. Present the game as a five-world wizarding progression through Common Room Practice, Moving Staircase Rush, Greenhouse Infestation, Forbidden Forest Edge, and Great Hall Night of 1,000 Charms, using this progression primarily through copy, HUD framing, procedural art, color evolution, and animated backgrounds rather than risky mechanic changes. Use code-native magical visuals like spell circles, floating candles, castle silhouettes, banners, runes, sparks, owl-feather motifs, potion haze, and pixie-like silhouettes. Maintain strong mobile readability, clear draggable targets, start and game-over overlays, and a polished magical HUD that makes the Harry Potter-inspired remix unmistakable without changing the protected drag, scoring, health, fail, and progression semantics.
